# 📋 Start Zimmer vaporizer

- **Checklist types:** Flame Effects
- **Area:** Propane area
- **When:** When the licensed Flame Lead authorizes flame-effect startup after a passed daily inspection

## What you need

- Licensed Flame Lead
- One trained spotter
- 📋 Inspect flame effect system
- 🔥 Zimmer Vaporizer — Propane area (see the map). Camp propane vaporizer identified as Zimmer in the source checklist, including its tank valve, relief valve, voltage display, thermocouples, and effect feeds.
- 🔥 Flame Effect Operating Procedure — At the flame-effect operator station. Current Flame Lead-approved system sheet naming every valve and control and stating the validated voltage, temperature, pressure, timing, startup, shutdown, and emergency-shutdown values for the actual installation.
- 🔥 Propane Leak Test Solution — Propane area. EASTMAN 65700B liquid gas leak detector, 2 oz, for LP-gas fittings.

## Ready before normal use

- **🔥 Flame Effect Operating Procedure:** The current revision is legible and approved by the Flame Lead.
- **🔥 Propane Leak Test Solution:** Enough solution is available for every connection being tested.

## Steps

1. Confirm that 📋 Inspect flame effect system passed today.
2. Confirm that every effect feed valve is closed.
3. Confirm that the release quarter-turn valve is in the closed position shown in 🔥 Flame Effect Operating Procedure.
4. Inspect the vaporizer guard and relief-valve outlet for damage, obstruction, or playa dust.
   - **IF/THEN:** IF the guard is damaged or the relief path is obstructed, THEN do not start the vaporizer.
5. Energize the vaporizer using the control named in 🔥 Flame Effect Operating Procedure.
6. Read the vaporizer voltage.
   - **IF/THEN:** IF the voltage is outside the approved range printed in 🔥 Flame Effect Operating Procedure, THEN de-energize the vaporizer and stop.
7. Wait until every thermocouple reaches the approved operating range printed in 🔥 Flame Effect Operating Procedure.
8. Slowly open the liquid-tank valve identified in 🔥 Flame Effect Operating Procedure.
9. Leak-test the energized vaporizer connections with 🔥 Propane Leak Test Solution according to the approved procedure.
   - **IF/THEN:** IF growing bubbles, propane odor, hissing, frost, or an abnormal reading is present, THEN complete the approved emergency shutdown and keep the system out of service.

## PASS when

- The daily inspection passed.
- The vaporizer voltage and every thermocouple are in their approved ranges.
- The liquid supply is open and no leak or abnormal reading is present.

## Finish

- Before marking PASS, return each used item to its location and leave it ready for the next person.
- Collect all MOOP.
- If an item, instruction, or solution is missing or unclear, ask the Dominatrix.

### Leave items ready

- **🔥 Zimmer Vaporizer:** The vaporizer is either under continuous licensed operation or fully shut down according to its approved operating procedure.
- **🔥 Flame Effect Operating Procedure:** The procedure remains at the operator station.
- **🔥 Propane Leak Test Solution:** The cap is closed and the bottle is stored upright.

### If an item is not ready

- **🔥 Zimmer Vaporizer:** Do not energize or open fuel to the vaporizer. Tell the Flame Lead.
- **🔥 Flame Effect Operating Procedure:** Do not operate the flame effect. Tell the Flame Lead.
- **🔥 Propane Leak Test Solution:** Ask the Propane Lead for replacement leak-test solution.

## Common problems

- **🔥 Propane Leak Test Solution:** **IF** The applied solution forms growing bubbles **THEN** Close the fuel supply, keep the equipment out of service, and tell the Propane Lead. Never use a flame to test for a leak.

## Who to ask

Flame Lead
